questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real unusual article?
questions.explanation: In 1932, the Australian military launched an unsuccessful campaign to cull thousands of emus that were destroying crops in Western Australia.

questions.prompt: In Elizabeth Loftus's famous 'Lost in the Mall' study on false memories, what percentage of participants came to falsely believe they had been lost in a mall as a child after suggestive interviews?
questions.explanation: The article describes the 'Lost in the Mall' study in which about 25% of participants developed false memories of being lost in a shopping mall as children after being exposed to suggestive information.

questions.prompt: In the assassination of James A. Garfield, how many days did Garfield survive after being shot by Charles Guiteau on July 2, 1881, before dying on September 19, 1881?
questions.explanation: Garfield was shot on July 2, 1881, and died from complications of his wounds and infection on September 19, 1881, approximately 79 days later.

questions.prompt: In 1990, members of the Jamaat al Muslimeen, led by Yasin Abu Bakr, stormed Trinidad and Tobago's Parliament and a TV station, holding the Prime Minister and other hostages. How many days did this standoff last before the insurgents surrendered?
questions.explanation: The coup attempt and hostage standoff lasted six days, from July 27 to August 1, 1990, ending when the insurgents surrendered in exchange for an amnesty.

questions.prompt: According to the Wikipedia article on the Observable Universe, what is the estimated diameter of the observable universe in billions of light-years?
questions.explanation: The article states that the observable universe has a diameter of about 93 billion light-years (28.5 gigaparsecs), based on the comoving distance to the edge of the visible universe in all directions.
